notice: Guidance describes common starting patterns, not mandatory rules. Race and attribute choices matter less than a coherent build, player execution, and encounter needs for most content.

sources.title: ESO New Player Guide: Character Creation

Arcanist.summary: Crux-driven class with strong beam damage, shields, support, and flexible ranged or melee setups.

Dragonknight.summary: Close-range pressure, damage-over-time effects, durable defenses, and strong group utility.

Necromancer.summary: Corpse-based damage, healing, and defense with deliberate setup and strong area control.

Nightblade.summary: Burst damage, executes, stealth-themed utility, and strong self-healing through offense.

Sorcerer.summary: Lightning, summoned allies, mobility, shields, and straightforward ranged damage options.

Templar.summary: Direct holy damage, strong healing, cleansing, and approachable melee or ranged rotations.

Warden.summary: Nature, frost defense, animal companions, healing-over-time effects, and broad group support.

Dark Elf.summary: A flexible damage-oriented choice with bonuses that work for both Magicka and Stamina setups.

High Elf.summary: A common Magicka-focused choice with offensive resource and recovery benefits.

Wood Elf.summary: A mobile Stamina-oriented option often chosen for sustain and movement-focused play.

Breton.summary: A forgiving Magicka sustain choice that can reduce pressure on resource management.

Orc.summary: A common Stamina and melee choice with offensive, Health, and mobility benefits.

Redguard.summary: A Stamina sustain option that fits builds using frequent weapon abilities.

Nord.summary: A common tank choice because its defensive passives support resistance and survivability.

Argonian.summary: A flexible support choice associated with healing, Health, and strong potion-based sustain.

Khajiit.summary: A flexible critical-focused option that can support damage or healing setups.

Imperial.summary: A durable flexible option commonly used for tanks and builds that value broad cost reduction.

damage.label: Damage
damage.summary: Focuses on defeating enemies efficiently. Resource, weapons, armor, and Mundus choices usually follow the selected Magicka or Stamina focus.

healer.label: Healer
healer.summary: Prioritizes healing, buffs, debuffs, and group resource support. Most traditional healer setups are Magicka-focused.

tank.label: Tank
tank.summary: Controls enemies, survives heavy damage, and supports the group. Attribute splits depend on final Health and resource targets rather than one universal formula.

support.label: Support
support.summary: A utility-focused setup that may mix damage, healing, buffs, debuffs, or encounter-specific responsibilities.

solo.label: Solo
solo.summary: Balances damage with self-healing, sustain, and survival so the build can operate without a full group.

magicka.armor: 5-7 Light with optional Medium/Heavy training pieces
magicka.summary: Common for spell-heavy damage and traditional healer setups.

stamina.armor: 5-7 Medium with optional Light/Heavy training pieces
stamina.summary: Common for weapon-heavy damage and many melee or bow setups.

health.armor: 5-7 Heavy with optional Light/Medium support pieces
health.summary: Common starting point for tanks. Final builds may move points into Stamina to keep it above Magicka or meet sustain targets.

hybrid.armor: Mixed armor based on the build’s dominant role and passives
hybrid.summary: For builds intentionally using both offensive resources. Many optimized builds still concentrate attributes in one primary pool.

pure_class.label: Pure class
pure_class.summary: Uses all three native class skill lines. This is the simplest starting point and can use Class Mastery after the native lines meet its requirements.

subclass.label: Subclassing
subclass.summary: Keeps at least one native class line and replaces one or two slots with foreign class lines. Only one line may come from each foreign class.

flexible.label: Flexible / undecided
flexible.summary: Starts pure class but records that the author expects to add alternatives later. The saved active configuration still contains exactly three concrete lines.
